question: Which type of reproduction is seen in Spirogyra?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fragmentation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Fragmentation** is a type of asexual reproduction where an organism breaks into two or more pieces, each of which grows into a new individual.
 
• In **Spirogyra**, fragmentation occurs naturally when the filament breaks into smaller pieces due to mechanical damage or environmental stress.
 
• Each fragment of Spirogyra contains a number of cells, and each fragment can grow into a new, independent filament.
 
• This method of reproduction allows Spirogyra to rapidly increase its population in favorable conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asexual Reproduction:** A type of reproduction that does not involve the fusion of gametes and results in offspring that are genetically identical to the parent organism.
 
• **Binary Fission:** A form of asexual reproduction seen in prokaryotes, where the cell divides into two equal halves, each becoming a new organism.
 
• **Vegetative Propagation:** A form of asexual reproduction in plants, where new individuals arise from vegetative parts such as roots, stems, or leaves.
 
• **Budding:** A form of asexual reproduction where a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud due to cell division at one particular site.
 
• **Spirogyra:** A genus of filamentous green algae of the order Zygnematales, known for its spiral chloroplasts and found in freshwater habitats.
